question: Which of the following is the correct product formed by the combination reaction of calcium oxide with water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Calcium hydroxide**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct product formed by the combination reaction of calcium oxide (CaO) with water is Calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)
 
• When calcium oxide reacts with water, it forms calcium hydroxide, which is commonly known as slaked lime. 
 
• The chemical reaction is:CaO+H₂O→Ca(OH)₂
 
• This is a typical combination reaction where two reactants combine to form a single product. 
 
• Calcium hydroxide is used in various industrial processes, such as water treatment and in the production of lime for construction​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Calcium Carbonate (CaCO₃)
 
 
• Calcium carbonate is not formed by the combination of calcium oxide with water. Instead, it is typically produced when calcium hydroxide reacts with carbon dioxide (CO₂). The reaction would be:
 
• Ca(OH)₂+CO₂→CaCO₃+H₂O
 
• Calcium carbonate is commonly found in nature as limestone and is used in various industries like construction and agriculture.
 
 
 
• Calcium Bicarbonate (Ca(HCO₃)₂)
 
 
• Calcium bicarbonate is not directly formed by the combination of calcium oxide with water either. It forms when calcium carbonate dissolves in carbonic acid or in water containing dissolved CO₂. The reaction is:
 
• CaCO₃+CO₂+H₂O→Ca(HCO₃)₂
 
• This compound is important in natural processes, such as the dissolution of limestone in water to form hard water.
